correctness.rationale: The prefix-count recurrence Z(j)=j−Z(floor(j/2)) yields the base-four weights 0,1,−1,0. In a carry-free addition of m_t, the increments are −2 to +1, with extremes realized at i=m_t and i=0. A remaining carry costs a digit with increment zero, offsetting the one higher-tail increment. Lower equality then requires the first carry at the last digit, because a digit receiving a carry cannot contribute −2; for t=1 its initial 3 string ends at a digit 1, giving odd valuation of i+1. At upper equality a carry from digit zero must persist with +1 increments until its higher increment at a 0 or 2, yielding even valuation. Thus the extreme factors have the required initial bits. Recurrence and unit sliding steps supply each interior zero count with both initial bits. Palindromic prefixes give reversal closure, so the terminal endpoint at even source starts adds no vectors. The arbitrary-length carry bound is logarithmic and the geometric subsequence gives the matching lower running maximum. A separate check in /workspace/branches/5728e89d-7db6-44fb-bb13-de493e568f0a/independent_spectrum_check.py and independent_spectrum_check_output.txt matched the exact spectra at all starts 0–131071 for t=1–7; this is finite corroboration only. The frozen code and its log were inspected, not executed.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For a p-factor of length n, its x-factor of length n−1 contains j nonzero letters exactly when the p-factor has j transitions and j+1 runs. When n is even, endpoints cannot both be 1 since all 1s occur at odd indices. Thus j=2z gives (z+1,z) and j=2z−1 gives (z,z), including the case j=0. For arbitrary n a given j yields at most two vectors. The attainable j form an interval by the zero-count sliding property used in the proof of Proposition 20.
